notes: 8. 6:00 PM - Public Meeting to Consider a Proposed Zoning Amendment 8.1 Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of the public meeting is to present the proposed by-law amendment and to receive public input prior to making a decision. The Township’s File Number for this application is RZ07/23.

Mayor Watters stated the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to change the zoning from “A” Agricultural and “EP” Environmental Protection to “A” Agricultural Exception and “EP” Environmental Protection on the retained parcel to restrict residential uses, and to permit a reduced lot frontage on the severed parcel. The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to implement zoning regulations necessary to facilitate a farm dwelling surplus severance.
The zoning amendment is a condition of approval of the County of Wellington Land Division Committee Application B19-23.

If a person or public body does not make oral submissions at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT).

If a person or public body does not make an oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

If you wish to be notified of the adoption of the proposed zoning by-law amendment, you must make a written request to the Clerk, Township of Centre Wellington, 1 Macdonald Square, Elora, Ont., N0B 1S0.
K. O'Kane, Municipal Clerk, advised the notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies, and public bodies on or before August 31, 2023.
Also, a copy of the notice was advertised in the Wellington Advertiser on August 31, 2023.
Presentation: Hailey Keast, Planning Technician, Van Harten Surveying Delegations:
Richard Wright, the applicant, indicated very few changes would be made to the property through the proposed amendment. His family has farmed the land for 25 years and will continue to farm the land.
No comments from Council.

notes: County Councillor Steve O'Neill provided an update on the Ridewell program, indicating approximately half of the rides are within the five- dollar minimum trip, and that 44% of all rides end in Centre Wellington.
Ridewell is currently operating as a pilot program and will undergo a service review in 2024. He further indicated the upgrades to the Elora Transfer Station will be completed in 2024.

items.title: 2023 Council Remuneration: Market Review
notes: Report from Rashid Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer R. Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer, provided an overview of the report stating the Township received data from 11 of 13 municipalities that were contacted for the market review. The review demonstrated the salaries for the mayor and councillors are significantly lower than the comparator municipalities.

In response to a question, Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer indicated the result of this decision will be presented in the 2024 budget, and staff would perform a market review of mayor and council salaries on a four-year basis.

items.title: Decision Report OPA01/22 and RZ17/22. 350 Wellington Road 7, Elora
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
Councillor Wilton excused herself from the meeting.

B. Salmon provided an overview of the property and the proposed development. He indicated the plan shows 271 units but that could vary up to a maximum of 280 units. A primary goal of the development is to have several live-work units that would be appropriate in a residential neighbourhood.
In response to a question, B. Salmon indicated a desire to have a multi- use path instead of a traditional sidewalk to keep cyclists off of the heavily trafficked highway.

items.title: Subdivision Agreement, Draft Plan of Subdivision 23T-18005 (Pastures
notes: Edge)
Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
B. Salmon provided an overview of the property, noting the proximity to a gravel pit. He indicated an environmental assessment has been completed by the Grand River Conservation Authority.

In response to a question, he indicated there is a warning clause as part of the purchase agreement and a warning will be included on Title to notify potential purchasers of the proximity of the gravel pit. He further indicated noise studies have been completed and the gravel pit is working towards noise mitigation measures.

motions.item_title: Notice of Intent to Designate - 255 Lamond Street, Fergus (Pierpoint Fly
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington issues a Notice of Intent to Designate the property municipally known as 255 Lamond Street, Fergus, also currently known as the "Pierpoint Fly Fishing Nature Reserve", as a significant cultural heritage landscape pursuant to Section 29 (Part 4) of the Ontario Heritage Act; and THAT staff be authorized to proceed with the notice requirements outlined in Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act; and THAT, if no objections are received within the prescribed time period, staff prepare and provide the designation by-law to Council for enactment as per Ontario Heritage Act requirements; AND THAT staff be authorized to proceed with establishing a Pierpoint Community Working Group through the Healthy Communities Advisory Committee to develop an interpretation and commemoration program and report back to Council as required.
